newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt lower, pressured by U.S. debt, dollar.
newsitem.headline: German debt lower, pressured by U.S. debt, dollar.

text.p: The German bond market continued to lose ground in late trade on Monday. Dealers said there was pressure on the long-end of the debt market after U.S. bonds eased.

The market was little moved earlier by a 1.4 percent month-on-month rise in pan-German June industry output, which was in line with expectations. The September Bund future was down 20 at 102.15 points, off a daily low of 102.01.
The debt market's woes were further compounded by the dollar, which had earlier traded strongly hitting a multi-year high of 1.8730 marks, but fell to about 1.8630 later on.
Speculation about what the Bundesbank might do to halt the deutschemark's decline also clouded sentiment.

"The bigger picture is that the mark is in secular decline and that's all thanks to prospect of the hard deutschemark being subsumed by a soft euro in the next few years," one British investment bank said in a research document.
"The only two things that the German authorities can do now to stop the rot is hike German rates till the pips squeak for the mark bears, or else to call time on EMU," the bank said.
Last Friday's sell-off had not turned into panic reaction, the bank said.
"Sentiment has already been badly scarred by market worries which have built in during the last couple of weeks over a possible interest reaction by the Bundesbank over the mark's meltdown," it said.

It said that the market could call the Bundesbank's bluff over using a threatened return to a variable rate repo as a deterrent to stop the mark's slide on August 12, when the first of the unannounced repos have to be set.
